inline_text:
This PR adds the September 2026 monthly report for the Security & Privacy Working Group and indexes it in `reporting/README.md`.

### Review requested from workstream leads

Leads, please check the bullet for your workstream under **Progress Against Objectives** and confirm the status is accurate as of the end of September. The report now reflects the 2026-09-29 meeting and the 2026-09-30 merges of [#9](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/9), [#8](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/8), and [#26](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/26).

### Month at a glance

- The Best Practices Guide merged via [#9](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/9) and is registered as a Draft deliverable. It is now a living document maintained through issues and PRs, with Fernando and Matthew as mandatory reviewers. Identity and trust topics are deferred to the Identity and Trust WG.
- The Threat Modeling Gap Analysis merged via [#8](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/8) as Draft v0.1 and is registered as a Draft deliverable. Dedicated threat modeling sessions start in early October.
- The Design Patterns Catalog landed its first four drafts via [#26](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/26): the catalog landing page and pattern template, Approval Checkpoint, Kill Switch, and Attested Isolated Runtime. [#11](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/11) closed in favour of #26, and [#28](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/28) is the first follow-up PR.
- Erin Farr's Security Best Practices Feature Matrix ([#20](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/20)) merged as the first best practices artifact on `main`.
- The Security and Privacy taxonomy terms went up for cross-WG review ([ws-taxonomy-landscape#56](https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape/pull/56)), the taxonomy workstream adopted a merge-after-quiet-period process, and roughly 40 drive-by PRs were dropped after outreach.
- The WG decided that PR authors do not merge their own changes into `deliverables/`, with workstream leads keeping fuller control over their own folders, to be documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- The WG agreed to trial an alternate-week APAC meeting tentatively at 10 pm Eastern, with Alex bridging both sessions.
- The cross-WG review checklist workstream has scope overlap issues open for each working group. Coverage is strong for three groups and missing for Agentic Commerce, Governance, and Workflow and Integration.
- Meeting attendance averaged about 19 across three September meetings (20, 19, 19), up from August's 18 and below the trailing three-month average of about 25.

### Decisions requested from the TC

- Whether the WG may establish a formal bidirectional information exchange with ETSI TC SAI on cybersecurity requirements for AI agents.
